title: Brimstone Vent (Submarine Ring of Fire 2006)
place: Brimstone Pit vent, NW Rota-1 submarine volcano, Mariana arc, western Pacific (ROV Jason II dive J2-192, ~554 m)
audio: track present in source (unchecked, probably music or silence); mute it
notes: A huge, billowing white eruption plume (sulfur-rich cloud, with small dark rock bits) churning upward from the erupting vent. It is continuous and the camera is nearly static, so any 3.4 s window works. Best seconds 0-10. Plume centre at x~0.55-0.6, filling the middle. The source is 640x480 (4:3) with a burned-in ROV data line at the top (J2-192 date/time/heading/depth, y~22-46 px). I cropped a 640x360 band at y=56, which removes that line completely, then upscaled 3x to 1920x1080 and resampled from 29.97 to 30 fps. It is soft, standard-definition footage, but the motion is dramatic. Dark circular camera-housing vignette in the corners. No people, no logos and no text left in the frame. (Avoid source 47-64 s, where the data line moves into the centre.)
fact_en: In 2006, scientists witnessed for the first time ever an underwater volcanic eruption, at the Brimstone Pit vent site on NW Rota-1; at Brimstone Pit, the pressure of 560 meters (1,837 feet) of water over the site reduces the power of the explosive bursts.
